title: QisMC: A Model Checker for QISKIT Program Debugging
abstract: We present QisMC, the first quantum model checker dedicated to debugging Qiskit programs. On the theoretical side, we introduce the notion of quantum-classical transition system and a quantum computation tree logic (qCTL) grounded in Birkhoff-von Neumann logic for modeling the behaviors and specifying the properties of Qiskit programs, respectively. On the implementation side, QisMC provides an end-to-end framework encompassing transition system generation, logical formula representation, and model checking algorithms, and it efficiently performs image computation based on decision diagrams. These methods and design principles give QisMC advantages over previous Qiskit program debuggers, including a unified property specification language, a fully automated and exhaustive verification process, and the ability to generate counterexamples. Extensive illustrative examples and benchmark evaluations demonstrate the practicality, efficiency, and scalability of QisMC in verifying realistic quantum programs.
summary: This paper presents QisMC, a novel model checker designed to formally verify quantum programs written in Qiskit. It achieves this by modeling the program as a quantum-classical transition system and employing a specialized quantum computation tree logic (qCTL). QisMC offers automated, exhaustive verification and generates concrete counterexamples when bugs are found, significantly advancing quantum software debugging tools.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of formally debugging complex quantum programs written in Qiskit, particularly those involving dynamic quantum-classical interactions like measurements and control flow.
main_result: It introduces QisMC, the first dedicated quantum model checker, which provides an automated, exhaustive verification framework for quantum programs.
method: The authors develop a quantum-classical transition system and a quantum computation tree logic (qCTL) to model program behavior, reducing the problem to classical CTL model checking solvable via decision diagrams.
model_or_system: The model is a quantum program executed on a quantum computer, modeled as a quantum-classical transition system. The state space involves quantum states (density matrices) and classical control flow variables.
key_observables: Safety, liveness, fairness, and invariance properties, diagnosed by generating a concrete counterexample execution path.
important_parameters: The complexity scales with the size of the quantum circuit and the depth of the control flow structure.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes the ability to model quantum operations and classical control flow constructs within the Qiskit API structure.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates a buggy Repeat-Until-Success (RUS) program, its Qiskit circuit, and the corresponding transition system. Figure 2 shows the overall QisMC workflow, detailing the qCTL logic and reduction to CTL.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical foundation by defining the quantum-classical transition system and qCTL, details the end-to-end QisMC framework (generation, logic, checking), proves the correctness of the model checking algorithm, and concludes with practical examples and benchmarks.
why_interesting: While focused on software verification, the rigorous formalization of quantum control flow and state evolution using temporal logic is highly relevant for understanding the theoretical limits and guarantees of quantum computation.
